title: Recommendation Priority Editor — sketches and backlog
content:
Context and problem statement:

Quick notes: this doc collects early sketches, interaction notes, and a prioritized backlog for a small feature: a Recommendation Priority Editor inside Optimize. Goal: give operators (SREs, platform engineers, product owners) a lightweight way to set business priorities and see how Optimize's batch/cache/quantization recommendations map to those priorities, with ability to tweak and persist policies per model/route.

Why this matters (short):
- Teams today get a list of recommendations (batch larger, enable kv-cache, try 4-bit quant) but no easy way to declare what tradeoffs they *care about* (cost vs latency vs quality).
- Ops end up ignoring recommendations or manually applying them across many routes. We want to reduce cognitive load and make the prescriptive changes repeatable and auditable.

Alpha concept (one-liner):
A compact editor that lets users assign weighted priorities (latency, cost, quality, reliability), preview ranked recommendation bundles, and commit a policy that can be applied at route/model/namespace levels.

Quick sketch descriptions (low-fi, hand-drawn reference):
1) Editor panel (left) + Preview list (right):
- Left: three vertical sliders (Cost, Latency, Quality) + a toggle for Reliability and a drop-down for enforcement level (suggest vs auto-apply). Sliders are 0-100 weights that auto-normalize.
- Middle: small histogram showing token distribution for selected route (sampled) — helps visually explain why batching size impacts latency.
- Right: ranked recommendation bundles: each row is a bundle (e.g., "batch=64 + enable-prefix-cache + 8-bit-quant"), with icons for estimated delta in cost/latency/quality. Expand row for example prompt-level diffs.

2) Drag-to-bucket UI (alternate):
- User drags recommendations into buckets: "Must keep quality", "Accept minor quality drop for cost", "Aggressive cost save". System computes implied slider weights. Good for quick ops.

3) Policy lifecycle panel (footer):
- Apply scope (route/model/namespace), schedule window, rollout strategy (canary percent, time-of-day), and safety checks (per-prompt QA set).

Microinteraction notes (important):
- Changing sliders updates the ranked bundles in <300ms (local heuristic), with a greyed-out server confidence score that revalidates asynchronously.
- When user hovers a recommendation, show tooltip with the most relevant reasons (e.g., "batching 64 reduces p99 by 80ms on high seq len 90% of requests").
- For quantization recommendations, give a small "quality sandbox" where the user can pick 5 seed prompts and see side-by-side outputs (A/B) and a diff score (BLEU/ROUGE-ish + embedding similarity).

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Users can adjust at least three priority sliders and see ranked bundles change.
- System surfaces estimated cost/latency delta per bundle (back-of-envelope numbers) and a confidence score.
- Users can save a policy scoped to a single route and view it in the policy list.
- There is a rollback action visible and a simple audit log entry created when policy is applied.

Data & API hooks we need (implementation notes for infra/dev):
- Endpoint to fetch sampled metrics for a route: token length distribution, p50/p90/p99 latency, cost per 1k tokens.
- Recommendation engine API: input = weights (cost/latency/quality), route metrics, model profile -> output = list of candidate bundles with estimated deltas + confidence.
- Sandbox runner: CI job that runs N seed prompts against baseline and proposed config, returns outputs and similarity metrics.
- Policy CRUD endpoints (create/read/update/delete), with scope metadata and change author.

Edge cases and open questions (brain dump):
- Multimodal models: quantization/kv-cache effects differ; how do we represent this? (Idea: show model tags and only offer compatible recs.)
- When confidence low: disable auto-apply, force canary and QA set. How do we compute "confidence"? require a min sample size or historical sim runs.
- Conflicting policies: route-level vs namespace-level; UI should show effective policy and origin-of-truth with breadcrumbs.
- Cost estimation variance: show ranges and explain assumptions (e.g., token price, baseline batch efficiency).

Backlog (prioritized, short bullets):
1) [P0] Weight sliders + local ranking UI + simple estimated deltas (no sandbox) — 2 week sprint.
2) [P0] Policy save/load + route scoping + audit log entry on apply — 1 sprint.
3) [P1] Sandbox runner integration (seed prompts + A/B view) + store sandbox results — 2 sprints.
4) [P1] Drag-to-buckets quick mode + mapping to slider weights — 1 sprint.
5) [P2] Canary rollout controls + schedule windows + observability links (console traces) — 2 sprints.
6) [P2] Model compatibility matrix and filtering (hide incompatible recs) — 1 sprint.
7) [P3] Bulk apply across routes + dry-run simulation — research spike.
8) [P3] Role-based access controls in editor (who can auto-apply) — 1 sprint.

Design language decisions & constraints:
- Keep the editor compact, target 1-2 rows of controls above the fold for quick ops.
- Color semantics: green = cost-save, red = quality-loss; neutral = reliability-impact. Avoid heavy use of red for subtle quality changes to reduce alarm fatigue.
- Icons for recommended action types (batch, cache, quantize) should be consistent with existing optimize iconography.

Telemetry & observability to add:
- Track slider-weight changes, applied policies, rollback counts, time-to-apply, and sandbox pass/fail rate.
- For any auto-applied policy, record pre/post metrics (p50/p99, token cost) for first 24h.

Notes for UX follow-ups (tasks for design):
- Produce one mid-fi prototype for the slider+preview flow and one alternative for the drag-bucket flow; put both in Figma and run 3 quick 30-min usability sessions with SRE beta partners.
- Create copy for tooltips and in-product explanations (short and scannable). Avoid heavy technical jargon for PMs/customer-facing users.

Sample dialog for the help text (short):
"Use the priority editor to tell Optimize what matters most. Drag the sliders to adjust tradeoffs — the recommendation preview will update instantly. Try 'canary' for low-risk testing"

Open action items (who/what/when):
- Asha: wireframes (mid-fi) v1 by 2025-11-06 (Figma link placeholder)
- Marcus: mock API contract for ranking endpoint by 2025-11-03 (add to OPT-4352)
- Riley: propose sanitization/sample size rules for confidence metric by 2025-11-05
- Diego: schedule 3 beta sessions with internal SREs week of 2025-11-10

Loose thoughts (notes-to-self-ish):
- Could we map existing Optimize prescriptions to a small taxonomy so recommendations are comparable across models? Might help when building ranked bundles.
- Consider a small "explainability" snippet per bundle that lists the top 2 telemetry signals that triggered the recommendation (e.g., high seq length, token-cost trending up, low cache hit rate).

References and links:
- Existing Optimize rec engine notes: CONFLUENCE OPT-3001 (link above)
- UX pattern inspiration: Chrome DevTools performance presets (for quick, named tradeoff profiles)

Rough timeline suggestion: prototype->internal beta->ship alpha (flagged) in 8–10 weeks if scope limited to sliders + save + preview.
